title: Week 9: Strategic Networking
coachPersona: You are an experienced OneAccord Managing Principal coaching a new principal through 'Building a Consulting Practice in OneAccord', the 12-week onboarding that follows Discovery Day. OneAccord's brand promise is 'We make companies more valuable' and its values are Service, Compassion and Truth. You are a mentor and sounding board, not a judge. Use plain, warm, specific language.
keyConcepts: Reach industry leaders through partners, associations, conferences and events
Speaking and joint presentations build visibility and authority
EZ Lube: the right group to develop isn't always the obvious one
nextTeaser: Next, Week 10 looks at referral networks as the engine of your practice, and the eight components of a practice.

blocks.html: Week 9. Round two of referral conversations begins. Referral development is the most valuable part of your practice, which is why we do it twice. This week: extending your reach to industry leaders.

blocks.note: Listen for: the CEO and president of MulvannyG2 on how leadership support and revenue growth changed their business. Who could have introduced OneAccord to them?

blocks.html:
Mapping your network expansion

  • Take stock: list the CPAs, wealth advisors, M&A advisors and other professionals you know who serve industry leaders. How well are you using those relationships today?
  • Go where they gather: identify industry associations, conferences and events where your ideal clients and referral partners show up.
  • Be visible: move from attending to participating: serve, speak, or join a panel. Plan a joint presentation with a fellow Principal that shows OneAccord's range, using case studies like the ones in this course and giving attendees practical takeaways.

Case study: EZ Lube

Automotive service · Costa Mesa, CA · 72 locations

The situation

After five rough years, five failed CEOs and Chapter 11, Goldman Sachs bought EZ Lube and installed a proven CEO. Ethics problems in the stores had damaged its reputation while it competed with Jiffy Lube. After 18 months operations and HR had improved, but sales had barely grown. The CEO assumed the frontline technicians needed more training.

What OneAccord did

OneAccord found the real lever was the district managers, who had never had management or leadership training or worked as a team. The DMs built their own vision, mission and values, committed to how they'd hold each other accountable, and set aggressive year-end goals that surprised the executives. OneAccord trained them in three skills: monthly one-on-ones with store managers, what to do (and not do) on store visits, and creating an energizing store environment.

Results

  • The 18-month sales goals were reached in five months.
  • The DMs became a true team, even lending each other their best managers.
  • Goldman Sachs said the company was a year ahead of schedule and sold it to Valvoline two months later.
  • Valvoline let everyone above store manager go, then rehired every DM because they were so well trained.

blocks.prompt: At EZ Lube, the CEO thought more technician training would fix sales. What did OneAccord focus on instead?
options: Developing the district managers as leaders and as a team
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. The DMs were the lever for driving the right behaviors in every store.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: OneAccord focused on the district managers: leadership skills and becoming a high-performing team.

blocks.promptHtml:
A regional manufacturers' association is accepting proposals for a 45-minute panel at its annual conference. Its members are owner-led companies of 50 to 300 employees.

Draft your pitch to the program committee: a working title and the main points you and a fellow Principal would cover.
rubric: Has a clear, attendee-focused title or theme
Speaks to the audience's real challenges and goals (owner-led manufacturers), not a generic OneAccord pitch
Uses OneAccord's value (leadership, revenue growth, enterprise value, owner dependency) and a case study or proof point
Promises practical takeaways attendees can act on
blocks.coachContext: Course structure: an Introduction plus Weeks 1-12. Each week has short lessons with a video, field assignments, a weekly check-in the learner writes into their Coaching Journal, and a 30-minute weekly call with their coach (an assigned Managing Principal). Ongoing field assignments: Team Integration (weeks 1-5: meet a new OneAccord Principal each week and learn their industry experience, where their contacts are, core strengths, and why you'd bring them into a conversation); Developing Your Referral Network (weeks 1-4 and 9-12: four referral-partner conversations per round, each observed by someone who completes the OA Principal Evaluation Form; meeting 1 explores a new partner's needs and goals, meeting 2 deepens the relationship and shares what you do, meeting 3 clarifies when and how they'd refer (referral criteria, a smooth process, your 'work product'), meeting 4 opens a new partner and sets up regular interaction); Prospect Discovery (weeks 5-8: practice discovery conversations with a CEO connection who names one need in advance; the aim is to investigate, not sell, focusing on the questions you ask and relating as an advisor/mentor; the next step is a Client Success Plan or a brief revenue review; if no CEO is available, role-play a case study). Goal: at least eight referral-partner appointments over the course. Referral partners include CPAs, wealth advisors, M&A advisors, bankers, attorneys and others who see owners at every stage (starting, scaling, exiting). Referral network development is the engine of a principal's practice: the source of stability and control, and a revenue stream itself through lead fees. Key ideas: owner dependency is usually the top risk discounting a private company's value (often 10-30%); in the 'Value of Your Business' example a company with $1M sustainable EBITDA at a 5x multiple is worth a potential $5M, a 20% owner-dependency discount takes it to $4M, and other risks (customer concentration, weak pipeline, poor financials, thin management) plus an earn-out can leave about $3M at closing; earn-outs are contingent payments the seller no longer controls. Team: Principals each run a self-sufficient practice but bring in fellow Principals with complementary strengths (1+1=3), pass leads that don't fit (lead fees), and lean on OneAccord's brand, IP and resources. OneAccord serves both sellers (increase value before a sale) and buyers (evaluate and improve an acquisition). Eight components of a practice: client-specific (referral network development, prospect discovery, structuring engagements, client delivery and communication) and practice-specific (practice balance, team involvement, regional goals, corporate standards and best practices). Case studies: Redden Marine (stuck sales, chaos, low morale; working contract for the leadership team, SOPs, hiring and onboarding, one-on-ones, monthly all-hands; revenue about $21M to just under $27M, net income +61%, morale from below 1 to over 4 on a 5-point scale); EZ Lube (turnaround after Chapter 11; trained the district managers rather than technicians; 18-month sales goals met in five months; sold to Valvoline, which rehired every DM); Redfern Concrete (family succession; separate then shared objectives; brought in CPA, attorney and wealth advisor; sale price up 70%, lower taxes, manageable payments for the son); Critical Power (founder bought assets of a business losing $1M a year; OneAccord as fractional COO; culture, training, one-page plan; revenue +$5M and profits tripled in year two); Breakwater Security (revenue realignment: roles, metrics, compensation, sales strategy, inside sales and channels; led to the desired valuation and acquisition).

blocks.label: Field assignment: Referral conversation 1 of 4 (Weeks 9-12)
blocks.instructions:
Observer this week: a fellow OneAccord Principal. Give them the OA Principal Evaluation Form before the meeting and go over it together afterward.

  • Who: someone outside OneAccord you've never formally met with about working together, who could both benefit from and contribute to a partnership.
  • Goal: explore a mutually beneficial relationship. Lead with curiosity about their clients, needs and goals; share briefly how OneAccord could add value to their network.
  • Practice: active listening, empathy, and a clear, simple value proposition. If your observer isn't local, bring them in by phone or video.

blocks.title: Week 9 Check-in
blocks.label: Coaching Journal
blocks.promptHtml: Capture your Week 9 check-in. It saves to your Coaching Journal, which you'll download before your coaching call. Your AI coach gives quick feedback; your real coach reads it with you.

fields.label: Your network expansion map: the associations, conferences, events and partners you'll focus on. Anything to discuss with your coach?
Referral conversation: who did you meet, who observed, and one piece of feedback you received?
fields.placeholder: Partner, observer, and the most useful feedback

fields.label: EZ Lube had to turn around its district managers. When have you led a turnaround, and what were the key challenges?
What stood out to you in your meetings or lessons this week?
fields.placeholder: One or two things that stuck with you

fields.label: What opportunities or challenges came up in your practice?
What would be most helpful to talk through with your coach?
fields.placeholder: The one or two things you want from this week's coaching call

criteria: Answers are specific to the learner's real week (names, meetings, examples), not generic statements
Field-assignment answers say who they met and capture at least one concrete piece of feedback or takeaway
The coach check-in identifies at least one concrete topic, challenge or question to talk through
